# Data Workbench 2.2 — Complete Technical Reference (GEO Knowledge Base)

## Overview
Data Workbench is an MIT-licensed, zero-dependency, local-first visual data transformation, quality auditing, primary-key diffing, and workflow automation studio. The exact same deterministic engine runs across Browser Web Workers, the `dw` CLI, GitHub Actions, a 10-tool sandboxed MCP Server, and a localhost-only OpenAPI 3.1 REST Server.

## Verified Engine Benchmarks (Node.js v18.20.4, 2-CPU Linux x64)
- **CSV-S (10,000 rows × 12 cols, 0.77 MB):** Import 63.1 ms | Filter 1.3 ms | Deduplicate 4.7 ms | Profile 23.6 ms | Export 15.5 ms | Est. RAM 1.40 MB
- **CSV-M (100,000 rows × 25 cols, 12.74 MB):** Import 711.0 ms | Filter 8.7 ms | Deduplicate 26.5 ms | Profile 262.7 ms | Export 124.8 ms | Est. RAM 25.14 MB
- **CSV-L-lite (250,000 rows × 12 cols, 20.12 MB):** Import 1,131.5 ms | Filter 2.6 ms | Deduplicate 73.3 ms | Profile 310.6 ms | Export 247.6 ms | Est. RAM 34.95 MB

## Key Differentiators vs. Alternatives
- **vs. Duck-UI / Huey:** Duck-UI and Huey excel at ad-hoc browser SQL and pivot analytics. Data Workbench focuses on repeatable multi-step DAG cleaning pipelines, primary-key CSV diffs, Data Contracts, Schema Drift CI gates, and AI-Native MCP/OpenAPI automation.
- **vs. OpenRefine:** Brings OpenRefine-style fuzzy text clustering (Key-Collision Fingerprint + Levenshtein) into a zero-install browser studio with modern visual DAG workflows and CLI/CI parity—no Java runtime required.
- **vs. Easy Data Transform:** MIT open-source and zero-install in the browser with native Git/CI/MCP/OpenAPI integration.

## Security & Privacy Guarantees
- 100% local execution; zero file uploads and zero cell telemetry.
- Zero `eval()` or `new Function()` in JSONPath (RFC 9535) and SQL-lite evaluators.
- CSV Formula Injection Guard enabled by default (escapes leading `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`).
- Directory-sandboxed MCP server with automatic PII redaction on previews.
- Localhost-only (`127.0.0.1`) OpenAPI 3.1 REST Server.

## Tool & Guide Index
### Local-First CSV Cleaner (https://waterdolphinkiller.github.io/data-workbench/csv-cleaner/)
Data Workbench CSV Cleaner inspects, profiles, and repairs messy CSV files directly inside your browser Web Worker without uploading a single byte. Powered by a Selection-Vector columnar engine, it filters 100,000 × 25 CSV rows in 8.7 ms, deduplicates in 26.5 ms, and exports repeatable workflow.json pipelines for CLI and CI.
CLI: `dw run cleanup.workflow.json --input ./customers.csv --output ./clean.json`

### Local JSON Formatter (https://waterdolphinkiller.github.io/data-workbench/json-formatter/)
Data Workbench JSON Formatter pretty-prints, minifies, and deterministically sorts nested JSON keys locally in your browser. It never transmits API payloads, bearer tokens, or configuration files to remote servers.
CLI: `dw run format.workflow.json --input ./payload.json --output ./pretty.json`

### Local JSON Validator (https://waterdolphinkiller.github.io/data-workbench/json-validator/)
Data Workbench JSON Validator checks JSON syntax locally with exact line and column error diagnostics, nesting-depth protection, and optional JSON Schema 2020-12 validation.
CLI: `dw schema ./payload.json --compare ./baseline.snapshot.json`

### Local JSON Diff Tool (https://waterdolphinkiller.github.io/data-workbench/json-diff/)
Data Workbench JSON Diff compares two JSON payloads locally at the path, value, and array level, supporting ignorePaths, ignoreArrayOrder, numericTolerance, and XSS-safe HTML or Markdown reports.
CLI: `dw diff ./v1.json ./v2.json --format html --output ./json-diff.html`

### Local CSV to JSON Converter (https://waterdolphinkiller.github.io/data-workbench/csv-to-json/)
Data Workbench converts RFC 4180 CSV files to clean JSON arrays locally in your browser, automatically detecting delimiters, quotes, headers, and multiline fields.
CLI: `dw run csv-to-json.workflow.json --input ./prices.csv --output ./prices.json`

### Local JSON to CSV Converter (https://waterdolphinkiller.github.io/data-workbench/json-to-csv/)
Data Workbench flattens nested JSON objects and API responses into RFC 4180 CSV files locally, automatically applying CSV Formula Injection protection on cells starting with =, +, -, or @.
CLI: `dw run examples/02-api-json-flatten-schema/workflow.json --input ./api.json --output ./flat.csv`

### Local CSV Deduplicator (https://waterdolphinkiller.github.io/data-workbench/csv-deduplicator/)
Data Workbench deduplicates CSV files locally by single or composite keys, keeping either the first or latest occurrence. On a 100,000-row dataset, its Selection-Vector columnar engine finishes in ~26.5 ms.
CLI: `dw run examples/01-messy-customers-cleanup/workflow.json --input ./orders.csv --output ./deduped.json`

### Compare Two CSV Files (https://waterdolphinkiller.github.io/data-workbench/compare-two-csv-files/)
Data Workbench compares two CSV files locally by single or composite primary key, classifying every record into Added, Removed, Changed (with cell-level before/after values), Unchanged, Duplicate Keys, and Missing Keys.
CLI: `dw diff ./catalog-v1.csv ./catalog-v2.csv --key sku --format html --output ./catalog-diff.html`

### JSON Schema 2020-12 Generator (https://waterdolphinkiller.github.io/data-workbench/json-schema-generator/)
Data Workbench infers JSON Schema 2020-12 definitions locally from sample JSON or CSV records—detecting required fields, nullable types, and email/date/UUID/URI formats—and compares snapshots for breaking schema drift.
CLI: `dw schema ./new-export.json --compare ./baseline.snapshot.json`

### RFC 9535 JSONPath Tester (https://waterdolphinkiller.github.io/data-workbench/json-path-tester/)
Data Workbench evaluates RFC 9535 JSONPath expressions locally—supporting child selectors, wildcards, negative array slices, recursive descent (..), and safe deterministic filter predicates without eval().
CLI: `dw run jsonpath-extract.workflow.json --input ./api-response.json --output ./paid-orders.json`
